rules.justification: Systolic BP ≥ 140 mmHg is the clinical threshold for hypertension.
Total cholesterol ≥ 240 mg/dl is the established cut‑off for hypercholesterolemia.
Peak exercise HR ≥ 100 bpm is a pragmatic proxy for tachycardia in the absence of resting HR.
ST depression ≥ 1 mm is the clinical threshold for a positive ischemic response.
Any major vessel involvement (≥ 1) is considered stenotic.
Involvement of two or more vessels is typical of non‑occlusive atherosclerosis.
Any symptomatic chest pain (typical, atypical, or non‑anginal) qualifies as chest pain.
Typical or atypical angina are the classic presentations of angina pectoris.
Fasting glucose > 120 mg/dl is a pre‑diabetes/ hyperglycemia threshold.
In practice > 120 mg/dl often flags individuals with Type II diabetes; the exact diagnostic cut‑off is slightly higher but this rule captures the clinical trend.
This ECG category is synonymous with LV hypertrophy.
Any non‑normal ECG finding (ST‑T abnormality or LVH) is considered an abnormal EKG.

rules.justification: Systolic BP ≥ 140 mmHg is the clinical threshold for hypertension.
Total cholesterol ≥ 240 mg/dl is the established cut‑off for hypercholesterolemia.
Peak exercise HR ≥ 100 bpm is a pragmatic proxy for tachycardia in the absence of resting HR.
ST depression ≥ 1 mm is the clinical threshold for a positive ischemic response.
Any major vessel involvement (≥ 1) is considered stenotic.
Involvement of two or more vessels is typical of non‑occlusive atherosclerosis.
Any symptomatic chest pain (typical, atypical, or non‑anginal) qualifies as chest pain.
Typical or atypical angina are the classic presentations of angina pectoris.
Fasting glucose > 120 mg/dl is a pre‑diabetes/ hyperglycemia threshold.
In practice > 120 mg/dl often flags individuals with Type II diabetes; the exact diagnostic cut‑off is slightly higher but this rule captures the clinical trend.
This ECG category is synonymous with LV hypertrophy.
Any non‑normal ECG finding (ST‑T abnormality or LVH) is considered an abnormal EKG.
